subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw own automated same-product archive import under `migrate` or `backup`, or should core stay limited to safer backup conversion/manual-restore guidance?
rationale: The request crosses CLI namespace, destructive archive writes, credentials, sessions, path remapping, and existing provider migration semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Scope A Core Migration Contract
options.body: Define a minimal first-party export/import or restore contract with preview, canonical path validation, secret policy, conflict handling, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Restore User-Driven
options.body: Add safer backup targeting or conversion plus clearer manual restore docs while avoiding an automated import command that writes archive-controlled state.

options.title: Route Most Scope To Plugins
options.body: Close or narrow core work if maintainers decide community tools should own cross-machine packaging and only missing plugin APIs should remain in OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Scope A Core Migration Contract
recommendation.body: Define a minimal first-party export/import or restore contract with preview, canonical path validation, secret policy, conflict handling, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans current-main CLI behavior, security posture, and product scope rather than a narrow code defect.
